  "text": "On Thursday, Ada found her father in the garage, sorting screws into a muffin tin.

“The removal men won’t take loose bits,” he said.

“They will if they’re in a box.”

He held one screw towards the window, then placed it with the others.

Ada lifted a folded blanket from the workbench. Beneath it lay the wooden height chart that had been screwed to the kitchen doorframe.

“You took it down.”

“New people might want to paint.”

The earliest marks were in pencil. Later ones had dates beside them in her mother’s blue handwriting. At fourteen, Ada had insisted on being measured without her shoes, then accused the floor of sloping.

“It won’t fit in your new kitchen,” she said.

“I know.”

“Or mine.”

“I haven’t asked you to take it.”

She put the blanket back, leaving the top uncovered.

Her father shook the tin. A screw jumped into the wrong hollow. He moved it back.

“Your brother said photograph it.”

“That’s an idea.”

“Yes.”

Outside, a van reversed along the lane. They waited until its warning beeps stopped.

Ada pulled out her phone and held it above the bench. Her shadow fell across the dates.

“Could you move it towards the door?”

He took one end and she took the other. In the daylight, she noticed a small mark above her last measurement.

“What’s that?”

“Your mother. Last Christmas.”

Ada lowered the phone.

“She reckoned she’d shrunk.”

“Had she?”

“A little.”

They carried the board to Ada’s car. It fitted between the seats, with the passenger seat pushed forward. Her father went back for the blanket."
